content.title: Selectors Choose the Target
content.hook: A CSS rule is only useful if it reaches the element you intended. The selector is the part that chooses the target.
content.context: You will start with three ways to choose elements: type, class, and id.
goals: Use type, class, and id selectors to target the intended elements without accidentally styling unrelated content.

content.title: ID selector

content.question: Which selector should you use when every paragraph on this page should share the same color?

feedback.correct: Use a type selector when the rule should apply to all elements of that type.
feedback.incorrect: Use a type selector when the rule should apply to all elements of that type.

content.question: Which selector should you use when only elements marked class="muted" should change?

feedback.correct: The dot marks a class selector.
feedback.incorrect: The dot marks a class selector.

content.title: A common mistake
content.text:
A learner writes muted { color: #777; } and nothing changes.

Why? The selector is missing the symbol that tells CSS this is a class.

content.question:
Match the target to the selector:

1. Every paragraph  2. Every element with class="card"  3. The element with id="hero"

feedback.correct: Type, class, and id selectors use different target descriptions. Choose the narrowest target that matches the requirement.
feedback.incorrect: Type, class, and id selectors use different target descriptions. Choose the narrowest target that matches the requirement.
